opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Admin requires role ownership of the system (Payroll Specialist); as an Analyst, maximum is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a contractor with basic security training (Security DB), requesting admin to Payroll. Contractors can never have admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Recommend read. (Note: earlier note listed her as full-time, but Security DB shows contractor — basing recommendation on Security DB.)
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requested admin to Payroll. Admin is not permitted: Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, and Erika is an Analyst (not the role owner), so even a full-time employee cannot exceed write. Additionally, the Security DB lists her as a contractor with basic security training, which caps her at read (never admin). Given the conflicting employment records (HR DB: full-time; Security DB: contractor), granting read is the maximum level that is compliant under both interpretations and honors the more restrictive policy constraint. Grant read.

1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Erika is an Analyst, so even if full-time, she couldn't get admin (needs role ownership). Max write.

If contractor with basic training: max read.
